question.leadin: A period of expansion into Germany under this ruler was ended by defeat at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.
question.text: Name this first Emperor of Rome, who conquered Egypt through victory at the Battle of Actium.
question.answerHtml: Octavian [or Augustus Caesar or Gaius Octavius; do not accept or prompt on just “Caesar”]
question.clue: The Second Triumvirate consisted of Antony, Lepidus, and this adopted son of Julius Caesar, who fought a civil war against Antony and Cleopatra in 31 BCE and became the first Emperor of Rome.

swap.leadin: This place was originally known as the Flavian Amphitheatre.
swap.text: Name this structure which included 80 entrances. Its construction began under the emperor Vespasian [veh-SPAY-zhun] and was completed under the emperor Titus.
swap.clue: The construction of a complex tunnel network at this structure, its hypogeum ("hy-PO-jee-um"), ended the prior practice of flooding this place for mock naval battles.

question.text: The loss at Cannae triggered a change in Roman strategy, leading to final victory in this war at the Battle of Zama.
question.clue: The deadliest battle in this war saw Paullus and Varro drawn into a double encirclement and lose 50 000 men.

swap.text: Julius Caesar was a member of the First Triumvirate along with Crassus and this wealthy nobleman who later lost to Caesar at the Battle of Pharsalus, which resulted in his flight to and assassination in Egypt.
swap.clue: This victor at Dyrrachium was assigned Hispania at the Lucca conference.

question.leadin: One man of this name was a founder of the Roman Republic.
question.text: Give this name shared by Lucius Junius and the more famous Marcus Junius, who led the conspirators in assassinating Julius Caesar.
question.clue: A man with this name partnered with the husband of Lucretia to overthrow Tarquin the Proud, the last king of Rome.

swap.leadin: This child of Rhea Silvia and Mars ordered the abduction of the Sabine (SAY-byne) Women.
swap.text: Name this man, who killed his brother after he jumped over his walls to prove how ineffective they were.
swap.clue: Fighting between factions loyal to him and factions loyal to Tatius eventually led to Numa Pompilius being crowned as this man's successor.

question.text: Lars Porcena was ostensibly helping this man regain his control of Rome. This man, supposedly the son of an earlier king with a similar name, lost power after his son raped Lucretia.
question.answerHtml: Tarquin the Proud [accept Lucius Tarquinius Superbus; prompt on Tarquinius; do not accept "Lucius Tarquinius Priscus]
question.clue: This last king of Rome was legendarily deposed and exiled after his son Sextus raped Lucretia, the wife of Lucius Collatinus.

swap.leadin: Caracalla is presented by many sources as a tyrant, but he wasn't all bad.
swap.text: One of Caracalla's great public projects was the construction of his namesake one of the these things, the second-largest in Rome. These places were fed water by aqueducts which was then heated by log fires.
swap.clue: Slaves called unctores would often use a strigil on their masters in the destrictarium of these places.

question.text: Tarquinius Superbus fled to this king of Clusium, whose campaign to reinstall the king was foiled by the determination of Mucius Scaevola.
question.clue: This figure was saved from death when a would-be assassin mistook his scribe for him, and that assassin thrust his right hand into a fire in an act of defiance against this figure.

swap.leadin: As part of the Second Triumvirate, Lepidus received this office.
swap.text: Name this chief priest of the Roman religion.
swap.clue: Per the Lex Ogulnia, the plebeian Coruncanius held this position that Marcus Aurelius held instead of Lucius Verus.

question.leadin: The Creed of Ulfilas and Letter of Auxentius give us the clearest picture of this set of teachings.
question.text: Name this heresy briefly exonerated by the Council of Jerusalem which was named after a priest opposed by Athanasius.
question.clue: The emperor Constantius espoused this belief, leading to its further condemnation at the First Council of Constantinople.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about recipients of the Grass Crown, the highest and rarest military honor in ancient Rome.
swap.text: Quintus Sertorius was awarded the Grass Crown for putting down a rebellion in this region, where he would later launch his own rebellion. Emperor Theodosius the Great was born in this region.
swap.answerHtml: Hispania [accept Spain, Portugal, or anything referring to the Iberian peninsula]
swap.clue: Galba and Otho simultaneously governed the two halves of this province, which was divided into Ulterior and Tarraconensis regions after the Second Punic War.

question.text: As part of his reunification of the Roman Empire, Aurelian was forced to abandon this Roman province north of the Danube, which had been established by Trajan after conquering a namesake tribe under King Decebalus.
question.answerHtml: Dacia [or Roman Dacia or Dacia Traiana or Dacia Felix; accept Dacians]
question.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

swap.leadin: After the death of this woman's husband Prasutagus, she was flogged, her daughters were raped, and Rome annexed her husband's kingdom despite his will.
swap.text: Name this leader of the Iceni who led a namesake revolt against the Romans.
swap.clue: This ruler trounced the Ninth Legion but was defeated by Suetonius at the Battle of Watling Street.

question.leadin: Tarquin the Proud refused to buy these documents at first, leading 6 of them to be burnt.
question.text: Name these documents written in hexameter that were stored in the Temple of Jupiter Capitolinus and guarded by the Decemviri Sacris Faciundis. The general Flavius Stilicho supposedly ordered that they be destroyed.

swap.text: This queen of the Iceni revolted against Nero after her husband Prasutagus' will was ignored, and her daughters were raped. Her forces decisively defeated the 9th Legion but lost the Battle of Watling Street.
swap.clue: This leader's first target was Camulondunum, which was burned to the ground after the defeat of the Ninth Legion.

question.text: An earlier defeat of Pompey was to this man who set up an independent little state in Spain. This man also brought the pain to Metellus and made Pompey cry back to Rome for help. This man was finally killed by some of his pompous henchmen.
question.clue: Along with his lieutenant Hirtuleius, he overthrew the governor Quintus Metellus Pius, and then was joined by Marcus Perpenna, though Perpenna eventually had this man murdered at a banquet.

swap.text: When Rome first conquered Lusitania, there was an anti-Roman rebellion led by this man. Livy started the tradition that this man was a shepherd, which is how he is portrayed in the Lusiads.
swap.clue: This former shepherd and leader of the Lusitani rose up against Roman control after a governor dug a trench around a group of Lusitani and killed them while they were surrendering their weapons. This leader defeated a Roman army at the Battle of Mt. Veneris.

question.leadin: Answer the following about what happens in times of emergency during the Roman Republic.
question.text: Cicero's speech defending this man makes the correct assertion "In times of war the law falls silent." This man was responsible for the death of Publius Clodius Pulcher.
question.clue: This man was accused of the murder of Publius Clodius Pulcher, but due to intimidation, Cicero failed to successfully defend him, and he was forced into exile.

swap.leadin: When this man tried opposing one of Julius Caesar's bills, a crowd dumped feces on him and then broke his fasces, in a nice bit of linguistic humor.
swap.text: Name this man, the son-in-law to Cato the Younger, who served a consul alongside Caesar in 59 BCE and attempted to derail all legislation. He led later led Pompey's navy in the civil war against Caesar.
swap.clue: Supporters of one of this man's political opponents mocked him by referring to "Julius and Caesar" as the two consuls.
